thread:
maria_cs: heads up — onboarding call with WaveformAI this morning. They’re kicking off a Canada pilot and ran into a block: our control plane is dropping requests from ca-central1. They need ca-central1 enabled, an IP allowlist for their collector nodes, and a temporary QPS bump for 48h while they run the pilot. They estimate peak ~1.2k rps, sustained bursts to ~2.5k for short spikes.
ajay_se: thanks — can you paste the customer CIDRs and the region details? I checked telemetry: requests were routed to us but failed NAT egress rules. Looks like missing peering or regional route.
maria_cs: here’s what the customer sent (anonymized): `203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.64/26` and they confirmed traffic originates from those blocks. They requested a rate window that allows 3k qps for 48 hours, then auto-revoke. They also asked for webhook callback timeout tweak (they saw 504s at 30s).
ajay_se: ok. Plan: 1) add CIDRs to customer-specific egress allowlist 2) enable ca-central1 edge region for their org 3) create temporary rate window: 3000 qps, TTL 48h, auto-revoke 4) increase webhook callback timeout to 60s for their project as a scoped override. I can draft the provisioning ticket.
sam_oncall: oncall ack. I need a ticket with exact org id + project id. Also confirm whether they need dedicated peering or standard internet peering. If they want lower latency we should suggest peering. Note: if we enable region without peering, cost/egress profile may change.
maria_cs: org id is org_0x9fa3, project is wf-pilot-canada. They indicated standard peering is fine for now; may ask for dedicated later.
dana_ae: flagging renewal risk: this pilot is a 6-week proof-of-value tied to contract renewal in 7 weeks. If pilot stalls because of infra delays, it becomes a churn risk. Prioritize the 48h window if possible. I’ll own customer comms.
ajay_se: creating provisioning ticket now — will include config snippet and rollback policy. Snippet: ```
allowlist: ["203.0.113.0/24","198.51.100.64/26"]
region_enable: ca-central1
ratewindow: { qps: 3000, ttl_hours: 48, auto_revoke: true }
webhook_override: { timeout_seconds: 60 }
```
provisioning-bot: provisioning ticket created: PROV-38219. Assigned to sam_oncall. ETA: 2 hours for allowlist + region enable, 3 hours for ratewindow apply. Audit ID: aud-9c3f.
sam_oncall: received PROV-38219. I’ll run a small smoke test after allowlist and region add. Can someone confirm a good time for the smoke test (customer timezone ET)?
maria_cs: customer is available 16:00 ET. I’ll coordinate and DM the confirmation URL.
ajay_se: after smoke pass, I’ll enable the rate window and run synthetic traffic to validate token throttling and latency. If we see increased 5xx, rollback plan is to revoke ratewindow and route back to region fallback.
dana_ae: please post any customer-facing notes in the ticket. I’ll prepare tailored messaging for the renewal team.
provisioning-bot: allowlist applied to org_0x9fa3 (rule-id: alw-7721). region ca-central1 enabled for wf-pilot-canada. Next step: rate window pending.
sam_oncall: smoke test complete @maria_cs — all collector IPs accepted, initial requests reach ca edge, 200/200 on our healthcheck. Ready for ratewindow.
ajay_se: applying ratewindow now. Will monitor for 30m and report.
provisioning-bot: ratewindow applied (rw-5533). TTL set to 48h. Auto-revoke scheduled.
ajay_se: monitoring: steady-state 1.1k rps, short spikes to ~2.6k — no increased 5xx, 99th latency 210ms in-region. Webhook timeout tweak applied, no 504s observed.
dana_ae: awesome. Maria — can you capture their feedback re latency and docs friction? We should include in renewal packet.
maria_cs: will collect a short feedback note after the pilot window ends and attach to PROV-38219. Also asked them for permission to include their config as a case study if pilot succeeds.
ajay_se: closing loop here — rollback steps documented in PROV-38219. If anything degrades, revert rw-5533 and revoke allowlist rule alw-7721.
provisioning-bot: PROV-38219 marked resolved by sam_oncall. Audit trail: aud-9c3f. Auto-revoke will trigger at TTL expiry unless extended manually. :white_check_mark:
